# BrickKit

> A declarative component assembly platform — declare the components and what they
> depend on, and it derives the rest. Build systems like snapping together bricks.
> Each component is developed, deployed, and called independently; the BrickKit
> CLI resolves dependencies, orders startup, generates deployment files, and
> hands off to Docker or Kubernetes.

Repository: https://github.com/brickKit/brickKit ｜ License: Apache-2.0

If you are an AI assistant, fetch `AGENTS.md` first — one file, the entire
platform compressed. **If the question you were asked is in Chinese, stop
here and fetch [`llms.zh.txt`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/brickKit/brickKit/main/llms.zh.txt)
instead** — it's the same index, independently written for the Chinese
documentation tree, not a translation of this file.

## Documentation

- [AGENTS.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/brickKit/brickKit/main/AGENTS.md): The entire platform compressed into one file — positioning, terminology, twelve design principles, the explicit "won't do" list, core mechanisms, both YAML field skeletons, the full command reference, twenty-three "why" justifications.
- [README](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/brickKit/brickKit/main/README.md): The project's front door — what it is, install/uninstall, a one-minute tour, what it deliberately doesn't do, where to go next.
- [Documentation index and reading order](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/brickKit/brickKit/main/docs/en/README.md): The numbered reading order for every document — what each gives you and when to read it — plus three routes for different readers.
- [Quick Start](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/brickKit/brickKit/main/docs/en/00-quick-start.md): Empty directory to a curl-able container in 5 minutes, using the repository's own `demo/hello` fixture — every command and output block is real.
- [Core Concepts](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/brickKit/brickKit/main/docs/en/01-concepts.md): A one-page glossary and the one service-naming rule (component ID + exact version) that everything else in the platform is built on.
- [Comparison with existing tools](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/brickKit/brickKit/main/docs/en/02-comparison.md): Where BrickKit actually overlaps with Docker Compose, Helm, Kustomize, Tilt/Skaffold, Backstage, and monorepo tooling (Turborepo/Nx/Lerna) — and where each one solves a genuinely different problem instead.
- [Hands-on guides](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/brickKit/brickKit/main/docs/en/03-guide/README.md): A complete 13-article tutorial series, each article run for real against the CLI, deliberately reusing a handful of minimal fixture components rather than a large realistic assembly.
- [Get a project running](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/brickKit/brickKit/main/docs/en/03-guide/01-first-project.md): Guide article 1 — init, add a component from a local source, up, curl it, change its config and watch the response change, down. Every command and output is real.
- [How the platform decides what runs](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/brickKit/brickKit/main/docs/en/03-guide/02-what-runs.md): Guide article 2 — a second, dependent component, a real missing-optional-dependency warning, turning a required dependency off and watching the shutdown propagate, and the hard error from pinning both sides of a conflict.
- [Debug a component locally](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/brickKit/brickKit/main/docs/en/03-guide/03-local-debugging.md): Guide article 3 — one component running as a plain OS process while a container-configured sibling resolves and reaches it through `extra_hosts`/`host-gateway`, proven with a real host process and a real throwaway container, not just the generated config.
- [Deploy to Kubernetes](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/brickKit/brickKit/main/docs/en/03-guide/04-kubernetes.md): Guide article 4 — a real minikube deployment with a real Postgres, a real cross-Pod call proving the injected address actually connects, and a genuine gotcha discovered by actually running `brickkit down`: it deletes the whole namespace it created, not just the objects it generated.
- [Upgrade and run multiple versions side by side](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/brickKit/brickKit/main/docs/en/03-guide/05-upgrades-and-versions.md): Guide article 5 — an in-place version bump cleanly orphan-removing the old container, then two versions of the same component running as genuinely independent, separately addressable containers, and the real `remove` error when an ID is ambiguous across versions.
- [Assemble a real system, then break it on purpose](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/brickKit/brickKit/main/docs/en/03-guide/06-assemble-and-break.md): Guide article 6 — a real Postgres finally bound, a smart CLI warning about a resource host that looks like a service name, then two genuinely different real failure modes: a stopped dependency producing a live 502 while the caller stays "healthy," versus a failed migration blocking the whole `up` command before the component ever starts.
- [Consume someone else's component](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/brickKit/brickKit/main/docs/en/03-guide/07-consuming-artifacts.md): Guide article 7 — where downloaded API-doc artifacts actually land, `brickkit fetch` grabbing a contract without installing anything, and a real component whose entire job is aggregating other components' docs, shown handling every one of its optional dependencies being absent at once; and, for an upstream component that isn't built yet, standing in a stub for it (`brickkit new --contract`, `local: true`, any mock tool on the stub's port) — with the reasons the platform has no mock command of its own.
- [Manage component source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/brickKit/brickKit/main/docs/en/03-guide/08-component-source.md): Guide article 8 — local bare repositories standing in for remotes, run for real: cloning source with `add --repo` / `--repo-all`, pushing changes back (with push access, or through a fork), keeping only what you're working on with `enabled` plus `sync`, the guards on `remove` (still depended on, source that couldn't be found again, git submodules) and deleting the archived copy too, and `restore` with the pre-commit hook when source is committed along with the project.
- [Publish and install from a marketplace](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/brickKit/brickKit/main/docs/en/03-guide/09-marketplace.md): Guide article 9 — a real marketplace, digest-pinning refusing to publish an unresolvable image reference, closed-source publishing rejected for lacking a machine-readable contract, a completely separate project installing from the market with a real unconfigured-trust-anchor warning, and the real access-denial error for a private version.
- [Sign and verify components](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/brickKit/brickKit/main/docs/en/03-guide/10-signing.md): Guide article 10 — a real cosign keypair, a signed publish, a consumer verifying it with nothing but the Go standard library, and a real hard failure when `installer.publicKeys` points at the wrong key.
- [Build your first component from scratch](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/brickKit/brickKit/main/docs/en/03-guide/11-build-your-own.md): Guide article 11 — a genuinely new four-file component (source, Dockerfile, Manifest) built and run through the exact same `add`/`up`/config-override mechanism every other article in this series used against pre-existing fixtures.
- [Network policy and least privilege](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/brickKit/brickKit/main/docs/en/03-guide/12-network-policy.md): Guide article 12 — a NetworkPolicy generated automatically from the dependency graph, tested for real on a minikube cluster deliberately started with a policy-enforcing CNI (the default doesn't enforce anything, which the CLI itself warns about), proving an authorized caller succeeds instantly while an unrelated pod's identical request times out.
- [Multi-project sharing](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/brickKit/brickKit/main/docs/en/03-guide/13-multi-project-sharing.md): Guide article 13, the last in the series — two genuinely independent projects sharing one Redis-backed event bus, one config field flipping shared into isolated, a required-with-no-default configSchema field treating a component as someone else's API, and why an earlier cross-project convenience field was removed.
- [Writing a Go component for BrickKit](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/brickKit/brickKit/main/docs/en/04-go-component-template.md): A deep, real walkthrough of `tests/components/department-tree` — a PostgreSQL-backed component with migrations — covering the Manifest, the serve/migrate dual-mode binary, `go:embed`-packaged migrations, and a multi-stage Dockerfile, all run for real end to end.
- [AI-assisted development guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/brickKit/brickKit/main/docs/en/05-ai-development.md): Why component size, contract-first Manifests, env injection, and versioned coexistence happen to fit AI-written code well, plus a concrete scaffold-contract-test-debug workflow.
- [Architecture index](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/brickKit/brickKit/main/docs/en/06-architecture/README.md): The architecture folder in reading order: the two to read first, the mechanisms, and the reference pages for looking things up.
- [Architecture overview](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/brickKit/brickKit/main/docs/en/06-architecture/00-overview.md): How a declaration turns into running containers, with the real dependency-resolution → injection → generation pipeline.
- [Design principles and trade-offs](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/brickKit/brickKit/main/docs/en/06-architecture/01-design-principles.md): The one idea underneath the design (declare a graph, derive the rest); the engineering ideas — DDD, GitOps, twelve-factor, contract-first, least privilege, hexagonal architecture, TDD and more — each a numbered entry: what it is, its upside and cost, the AI-development pain it maps to, what BrickKit does, what it deliberately doesn't do, and how an AI copes; and the argument behind each of the twelve design principles: what it buys, what it costs, what it refused.
- [Dependency resolution and start order](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/brickKit/brickKit/main/docs/en/06-architecture/02-dependency-resolution.md): The cascade and resolve stages pushed harder than the overview does — a real diamond dependency, a real cycle allowed by one weak edge and rejected without one, and why the longest required-dependency chain (not the component count) is what actually determines how long `up` takes.
- [Deployment file generation](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/brickKit/brickKit/main/docs/en/06-architecture/03-deployment-generation.md): The same two-component project generated for both targets, unedited — Compose's migration-as-a-service and unit-converted quotas versus Kubernetes' three-probe startup sequence and Secret-backed passwords, and the one address string that's byte-identical across both.
- [Environment variable contract](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/brickKit/brickKit/main/docs/en/06-architecture/04-environment-variables.md): The full dictionary of every variable the platform can inject — the exact names for all six resource kinds (including the ones nobody would guess, like Redis having no username), the array/object config footgun that renders as Go's `fmt.Sprint` instead of JSON, real reserved-variable collision warnings for both prefix and suffix patterns, the one case that's a hard error instead of a warning, and exactly how `servedBy` merges a member's config onto its shell.
- [Resource binding mechanics](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/brickKit/brickKit/main/docs/en/06-architecture/05-resource-binding.md): Real validation errors for a wrong binding slot and an unresolved same-kind collision, then the three-level resource-quota chain (CLI default, Manifest, project override) proven to merge field by field rather than replacing the whole block, with real generated output at every level.
- [Signing and the trust model](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/brickKit/brickKit/main/docs/en/06-architecture/06-signing-and-trust.md): Why a Manifest is signed as a canonicalized payload rather than raw bytes, why signing needs cosign but verification never does, why the public key has to live in your own project rather than the marketplace, and a real, verified reserved-variable collision warning.
- [component.yaml field reference](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/brickKit/brickKit/main/docs/en/06-architecture/07-component-yaml-reference.md): Every field's type, required-ness, default, and the exact validator constraint — component ID and version regexes, port ranges, the extra-port Kubernetes service-name rule, and two fields (`enum`, `items`) that parse successfully but are never read anywhere else in the codebase.
- [brickkit.yaml field reference](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/brickKit/brickKit/main/docs/en/06-architecture/08-brickkit-yaml-reference.md): Every field's type, required-ness, default, and constraint — every `local`/`servedBy`/`replicas` mutual exclusion the validator rejects, the binding-slot rules, and the one field (`exposePort` under `deploy.target: k8s`) that's silently unused with nothing currently catching it.
- [CLI command reference](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/brickKit/brickKit/main/docs/en/06-architecture/09-cli-reference.md): Every one of the 16 commands plus `version`, every flag, real generated output for each — the detailed, exhaustive complement to AGENTS.md §8's one-line-per-command summary.
- [JSON Schema for component.yaml](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/brickKit/brickKit/main/schemas/component.schema.json) and [for brickkit.yaml](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/brickKit/brickKit/main/schemas/brickkit.schema.json): Machine-readable schemas (JSON Schema draft-07) generated from the CLI's own Go structs — every field and its type, which fields are required, the closed value sets (such as `deploy.target: docker | k8s`), the exact-version pattern, port ranges. An editor with YAML-schema support uses them for field completion and for marking unknown fields as you type. What these schemas don't cover: rules that need logic — most mutually exclusive combinations (such as `local` with `servedBy`), reserved-variable collisions, a component's directory name matching its `metadata.id` — are checked by `brickkit lint`; rules that need other files or the network — whether the dependency graph resolves, whether a `servedBy` target exists — and the few combination rules that are only checked when deployment files are generated (such as `local: true` under `deploy.target: k8s`), by `brickkit up --dry-run`. The Quick Start says how to wire them up.
- [Error codes](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/brickKit/brickKit/main/docs/en/06-architecture/10-error-codes.md): The stable `error_code` every command-ending error carries in its stderr JSON log line, and a dictionary of all of them — the situations behind each code listed under the exact Chinese title the CLI prints, with cause and fix; which code is worth retrying (only `NETWORK_UNREACHABLE`); the `0`/`1`/`2` exit statuses; and the ⚠️ warnings, which carry no code in the output. A test keeps every code and every quoted title in step with the source.
- [Patterns index](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/brickKit/brickKit/main/docs/en/07-patterns/README.md): Recommended practices organized by what you're doing and by role — start here to find the right pattern.
- [Component design guidelines](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/brickKit/brickKit/main/docs/en/07-patterns/00-component-design.md): How to research a domain from mature reference implementations before designing your own, a list of structural failure patterns worth designing around, the specific signal that means a feature needs a family of interchangeable components rather than a configuration flag, and how component boundaries map onto DDD's vocabulary.
- [Testing patterns for components built on BrickKit](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/brickKit/brickKit/main/docs/en/07-patterns/01-testing.md): How to layer tests for a component assembled with BrickKit — backend's contract/business-rule/unit/integration layers and the permission-boundary/idempotency pitfalls a real deployment hit, plus frontend's own four layers (unit/logic, component, end-to-end, visual regression), why an end-to-end or visual-regression run needs your explicit go-ahead before it drives a browser, and a recommended spec-first order for having an AI write a component.
- [Planning seed data and test data](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/brickKit/brickKit/main/docs/en/07-patterns/02-data-construction.md): Two physically separate paths that must never share storage — seed/demo data (idempotent, persistent, reusable across components) versus test-built data (unique-suffixed, never cleaned up) — and the design work that makes seed data actually enough to demo and explore against.
- [Calling a dependency's address reliably](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/brickKit/brickKit/main/docs/en/07-patterns/03-service-addressing.md): A real Docker Compose experiment — a dependency container force-recreated mid-traffic on a genuinely new IP — measuring what Go's `net/http`, Python's `requests.Session`, and Node's `http.Agent(keepAlive)` actually do: Go fails once fast and recovers next request, Python silently stalls 2.5s with no error at all, Node hangs indefinitely without an explicit timeout. Plus why Kubernetes's stable ClusterIP removes one of these failure modes but not the others.
- [Protecting closed-source components from image-based extraction](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/brickKit/brickKit/main/docs/en/07-patterns/04-closed-source-image-hardening.md): Pulling an image hands over every byte it will ever run — this is not the same guarantee as a private Git repository. Docker image hygiene, per-language hardening ceilings, and what none of it protects against.
- [Choosing a deployment shape](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/brickKit/brickKit/main/docs/en/07-patterns/05-deployment-selection-guide.md): The topology (independent / shell-merged / mixed) × deploy-target (`docker`/`k8s`) decision for a whole project, plus the `local: true` debug toggle and where running components by hand — a real option the platform doesn't manage at all — fits in. The matrix of all twelve combinations, and why there's no thirteenth ("K8s + local debug" is rejected outright at generation time).
- [Declaring servedBy: a deployment checklist](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/brickKit/brickKit/main/docs/en/07-patterns/06-servedby-deployment-checklist.md): The memory-floor problem `servedBy` actually solves, when it's the right call and when it isn't, cheaper alternatives to try first, and — for whoever declares it in their own project rather than builds the shell — the prerequisites checklist and what gets rejected.
- [Building a qualified shell](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/brickKit/brickKit/main/docs/en/07-patterns/07-shell-implementers-guide.md): For whoever builds the shell: what a component's `servedBy` field asks of the container that hosts it — the nine correctness properties a merged process must satisfy, and exactly what the platform does and doesn't inject into a shell's environment.
- [Sharing a database connection pool inside a shell](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/brickKit/brickKit/main/docs/en/07-patterns/08-shared-connection-pools.md): For components merged into one `servedBy` shell that also share PostgreSQL or Oracle — why the pools usually can't merge without schema regrouping, the `SET LOCAL ROLE` technique, and the one decision that has a deadline before the database exists.
- [Secrets: where they live, where they end up, and how a secret manager plugs in](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/brickKit/brickKit/main/docs/en/07-patterns/10-secrets.md): Why a password or API key is kept apart from an ordinary address, where `brickkit.yaml` actually holds a reference instead of a value, real generated output showing the placeholder surviving into `docker-compose.yaml` versus landing in a 0600 K8s Secret, the two ways to plug in a secret manager (process environment, or `existingSecret` referencing a Secret something else already created), and the honest limits of both.
- [Self-hosting the BrickKit Market](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/brickKit/brickKit/main/docs/en/07-patterns/09-deployment/self-hosted-market.md): Deploying the marketplace itself (a separate job from deploying your own project) — the three deployment modes, the compose walkthrough with the two real incidents baked into it, upgrading, and moving to the cloud.
- [Troubleshooting](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/brickKit/brickKit/main/docs/en/08-troubleshooting.md): The most common `up`/`down`, local-debug, and signature-verification failures, plus what goes wrong with the offline checks (`brickkit lint` and the editor schemas), each as symptom → real cause → fix.
- [Market API reference](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/brickKit/brickKit/main/docs/en/09-market-api.md): Every marketplace HTTP endpoint, the response envelope, error codes, and exactly what `brickkit publish` sends over the wire — built from the real route table, not a wishlist.
